patterns.note: Subtitle Style Workbench uses a dominant 16:9 preview and bounded right-side inspector.
Inspector sections and advanced controls are disclosed through semantic details groups instead of one flat parameter stack.

mechanism: Preview and inspector are sticky within the layout workspace on wide layouts; inspector owns bounded vertical overflow.
Inspector header/actions remain reachable while parameter content scrolls.
Advanced semantic groups use details/summary disclosure with stable underlying control identity.
Mobile/coarse-pointer rules return the inspector to static full-width document flow.
implementation_effects: The preview remains visually dominant rather than sharing equal width with a long form.
The inspector stays compact and scrollable on wide screens.
Low-frequency advanced controls do not permanently occupy the same hierarchy as primary controls.
Narrow layouts preserve reachability by stacking preview and controls vertically.
responsive_contract: Desktop/large layout: flexible preview + inspector clamped to 390–460px.
At max-width 960px, or coarse pointer up to 1200px, presentation becomes a one-column flow and the inspector becomes static.
Control identity and export behavior are preserved across presentation changes.

validation_files.kind: production UI contract tests for split geometry, sticky/static fallback and workbench structure

limitations: Implementation lives in a large application HTML file rather than a reusable component package.
This record proves production source and contract tests, not a captured production visual state.
